meta.name: Perch
meta.organising_principle: Every surface is ruled like a ledger: a hairline under each heading and a mono index label in the top-left corner. Even without the logo, our work is recognisable because it looks like a page from a well-kept book.
meta.reference_points: Muji signage, Monocle's charts, a hotel's front-desk ledger, Swiss railway timetables. Not: SaaS gradient marketing, crypto dashboards, boutique-hotel gold foil, illustrated blob people.
meta.weird_detail: The mono index label in the top-left of every surface (FIG. 04, REF 2026-A). It is never explained and never removed.

inverse._use: Text on inverse and accent surfaces.

hairline._use: Table rules and dividers. The ledger line.

warning._use: Needs attention. Background clay.100. Never decorative.

base._note: moss.600 fails contrast on dark. Always step up.

_rules: Accent appears at most twice per viewport: one primary action and one active nav state. Everything else is ink, paper or hairline.
The page is never pure white and the ink is never pure black. #FBF7F1 and #241E1A carry the whole brand.
State colours are never decorative. Clay means something needs attention; if nothing does, nothing is clay.
Charts run moss.600, slate.600, clay.500, ink.500, moss.300. Never a rainbow, never more than five series.
In dark mode, separate raised surfaces with border.base. Shadows are invisible on dark.

webfonts._use: The one stylesheet that loads every brand face on the web. The brand site and any web build link it once in <head>.

display._use: h1 and h2, pull quotes, deck titles, the wordmark. Never body, never UI. WONK on above 24px, off below.

text._use: All body copy, all UI, h3 and below.

mono._use: The index labels, confirmation numbers, tabular figures in dense tables. This is the device.

scale._note: Display sizes break the ratio deliberately. They are set by eye.

display._use: Hero and deck cover. One per page.

h1._sample: Thursday looks busier than last week

lead._use: One paragraph under an h1. Never two.
lead._sample: The three numbers you run the house on, every morning.

body._use: Default for prose. 1.125rem, not 1rem — GMs read this on a desk monitor. Measure capped at 68ch.
body._sample: Occupancy dropped four points against the same week last year.

label._use: The index label, form labels, table headers. Never a sentence.

metric._use: The one big number on a dashboard card. Tabular figures always.

quote._sample: We stopped guessing on a Monday.

platform.web: Both families. Fraunces above 1.375rem only; Inter everywhere else.
platform.ios: Fraunces bundled, display above 24px only. SF Pro for all UI, so Dynamic Type keeps working.
platform.android: Fraunces bundled, display above 24px only. Roboto for all UI.
platform.email_pdf: System serif and sans. Never a webfont — it will not load in a mail client, and a PDF needs the file embedded.
platform._rule: The brand face never appears below 24px in a native app. If a screen needs character below that size, it comes from colour or spacing, not from a second face.
platform._why: Chosen over one-face-everywhere because there is nobody to own font loading and the Dynamic Type ladder in the app, and GMs read this on a phone in a corridor.

_rules: Never more than two type sizes in one card. If you need a third, split the card.
Body text is never centred. Exception: empty states, auth screens, deck covers, the 404.
Fraunces is never used below 1.375rem and never at weight 700.
Measure is capped at 68ch. A full-bleed paragraph is a bug.
Numbers in tables and metrics use tabular figures and are right-aligned.

space._note: Absolute numeric scale. Never invent an intermediate value — pick the nearer step.
_rules: Section rhythm is space.9 on desktop and space.7 below 768px.
The gap around a group is always at least two steps larger than the gap inside it.
Density setting: standard. Body 1.125rem, section padding 6rem, component padding 1.5rem.
Pill radius is for tags, avatars and count badges only. A pill-shaped button is off-brand.
Tables and data grids are square. Sharpness signals precision.
Nested radii decrease inward: an 12px card holds an 8px control, never another 12.

shadow._philosophy: Perch prefers a 1px hairline to a shadow. The ledger line is the device; a shadow competes with it.
shadow.dark_note: Shadows are invisible on dark. Use border.base to separate raised surfaces.

_rules: Nothing animates for longer than 320ms.
No bounce, no overshoot, no spring. Perch does not bounce.
Entrances fade and rise 12px. Nothing flies in, slides across or scales from zero.
Honour prefers-reduced-motion: collapse duration to zero, keep opacity.

principles.name: Calm
principles.rule: Nothing moves unless it explains a change. A number that updated may fade in; a card that did not change stays still.

principles.name: Quick
principles.rule: Everything finishes inside 320ms. A GM with eleven minutes should never wait for an animation.

principles.name: Straight
principles.rule: Things fade and rise 12px. No bounce, no spring, no overshoot — the house does not bounce.

motion.temperament: Quiet and quick. Motion confirms; it never performs.

_rules: Content is left-aligned to a 12-column grid. One deliberate asymmetric split per page — 7/5, not 6/6.
Never centre a layout except for empty states and auth screens.
Margin is space.7 (3rem) on desktop and space.5 below 768px. The gutter is space.5 on every size.

formats.name: Web hero
formats.rule: Display line on the left five columns, one image on the right seven. Never centred.

formats.name: Social square
formats.rule: Accent fills the canvas. One sentence, the index label top-left, the wordmark bottom-left.

formats.name: Portrait story
formats.rule: Paper ground. Photograph in the top half, the sentence below it, under a hairline.

formats.name: Slide
formats.rule: One idea per slide. Index label top-left, a hairline under the title, the number set in the metric role.

iconify._use: The Iconify set the site and any build renders from. Phosphor Light would be {prefix: ph, suffix: -light}.

icon.perspective: Straight-on or profile only. Never 3D, never isometric.
_rules: One library only. Never mix Lucide with another set, and never with emoji.
An icon without a label or a tooltip is a bug.
No emoji in product UI, marketing or headings.
Filled icons are reserved for the active and selected state. Everything else is outline.
One concept, one icon. Occupancy is always bed-double — never a person, never a percent sign.
A 16px icon beside 16px text is drawn at 18–20px to look optically equal.

logo.construction: Fraunces 400 at -0.03em tracking, the 'h' ascender shortened to cap height. That is the whole mark.
logo.clearspace: The height of the mark on all sides
_rules: Never recolour outside the three permitted values.
Never place the lockup on a photograph without a solid plate behind it.
Never stretch, rotate, outline, add a shadow to, or re-set the wordmark in a live font.
The mark alone is used at 32px and below, and as an avatar. Never as a decorative watermark.

art_direction._concept_use: The one line every shoot, layout and campaign is briefed against. If an image does not show the house working, it is not ours.

principles.name: Ruled, not decorated
principles.rule: Structure carries the brand. A hairline under every heading and the index label in the corner do more than any colour or ornament.

principles.name: Colour marks consequence
principles.rule: Moss appears where something can be acted on. Everywhere else the page is paper, ink and hairline. Clay appears only when something needs attention.

principles.name: The real building
principles.rule: Every image is a real property on a real morning. No renders, no stock interiors, no product floating in a void.

formula.subject: Back of house and quiet rooms: linen cupboards, the front desk at 07:00, a corridor between turns. People only as staff, mid-task.
formula.light: Available light from a window, mid-morning. Never flash, never golden hour.
formula.colour: Paper and ink dominate every composition. Moss appears once at most, and only where it is real in the scene.
formula.framing: Eye level, straight on. Square to the architecture. One clear subject, generous negative space on the side the type will sit.
formula.type_on_image: Never. Type sits on paper beside or below the image, under a hairline.

hierarchy.job: Carries the brand on every surface. The default when in doubt.
Proves the building is real. Marketing and onboarding only.
hierarchy.share: One image per surface at most

hierarchy.job: Show the product's answer. Product and sales material.
hierarchy.share: Where there is a number to show

art_direction.weird_detail: The mono index label in the top-left of every surface (FIG. 04, REF 2026-A). It is never explained and never removed.
_rules: One image per surface, at most. Two photographs side by side read as a hotel brochure.
Type never sits on a photograph. If a headline must be near an image, it sits on paper beside it, under a hairline.
The index label appears in the top-left of every substantial surface, including social, slides and print.
When nothing in this list decides it, pick the option that looks more like a well-kept ledger and less like an app.

attributes.means: Short words for real things. 'Your occupancy dropped four points last week' beats 'Occupancy metrics indicate negative variance.'
Give the number, the date, the room. Never 'significantly', 'dramatically', 'a lot'.
We speak like a good head of housekeeping, not a chatbot. No exclamation marks, no 'Hey there'.
We never manufacture urgency. No countdowns, no 'limited spots', no red banner for a non-urgent thing.

voice.person: We and you. Never 'Perch does X' in product copy — 'We'll email you when the forecast is ready.'
voice.tense: Present. Past only for things that happened.
voice.sentence_length: Average under 18 words. Vary it. One-word sentences are allowed.
voice.reading_level: Grade 9. Users are hoteliers, not analysts.
voice.locale: en-GB. -ise not -ize. DD Month YYYY. 24-hour clock. £ before the number, no space. No Oxford comma.
voice.capitalisation: Sentence case for every heading, button, label and menu item. 'Save changes', not 'Save Changes'.
voice.punctuation: No exclamation marks in product UI or marketing. Spaced en dash, not em dash. Ellipsis only for truncation.

avoid.solution: name the thing — the forecast, the report
avoid.AI-powered: say what it does — 'forecasts your occupancy'

voice.core: en-GB · Sentence case everywhere · No exclamation marks

messaging.one_liner: Perch turns your PMS data into the three numbers you actually run the house on.
messaging.elevator: Independent hotels run on spreadsheets and instinct. Perch connects to your property management system and gives the GM a single daily read on occupancy, rate and the week ahead — with the reasons behind each move, not just the chart.
messaging.positioning: For independent hotels of 20 to 120 rooms who cannot justify a revenue manager, Perch is operations intelligence that reads their existing PMS and answers the daily questions. Unlike enterprise revenue management platforms, which need a specialist to operate.

pillars.name: Plain answers
pillars.proof: Every number links to the bookings that produced it.

pillars.name: No new work
pillars.proof: Connects to your PMS in ten minutes. No data entry, ever.

pillars.name: Built for the desk
pillars.proof: Designed for a GM with eleven minutes, not an analyst with an afternoon.

proof_points: Used by 340 independent properties across the UK and Ireland.
Connects to Mews, Cloudbeds, Guestline and Apaleo.
messaging.boilerplate: Perch is operations intelligence for independent hotels. Founded in 2023 and based in Bristol, Perch connects to a property's existing PMS and gives general managers a daily read on occupancy, rate and the week ahead. perch.co

photography.point_of_view: The camera is a guest who arrived early: it notices how the house runs before anyone performs for it. Documentary, never staged.

types.name: The house
types.job: Rooms, corridors and the front desk, empty or nearly so. Proves the product is about real buildings.
types.prompt: An empty guest room in a small independent British hotel between guests: a made bed with white linen, a wooden chair, a sash window, morning light falling across the floor. Shot square to the wall, eye level, space on the left side.

types.name: At work
types.job: Staff mid-task: folding, checking in, reading a printout. Shows who the product serves.
types.prompt: A housekeeper in her fifties folding white towels on a trolley in a hotel corridor, mid-task, looking down at her hands, not at the camera. Plain uniform, real and unglamorous.

types.name: Detail
types.job: Close objects that carry the ledger idea: a key rack, a handwritten rota, a stack of folded linen.
types.prompt: Close detail of an old wooden key rack behind a hotel front desk, brass room keys on numbered hooks, a handwritten paper rota pinned beside it.

recipe.light: Available window light, mid-morning. Soft, directional, never flash, never golden hour.
recipe.framing: Medium or wide, eye level, square to the architecture. Verticals stay vertical.
recipe.subject_state: Mid-task or empty. Nobody looks at the camera. Nobody smiles at a laptop.
recipe.casting: Real staff of real properties, of every age. Never models, never guests posing.
recipe.colour: Natural, slight warm balance (+200K). Paper whites stay warm, never blue.
recipe.depth: Moderate. The room stays readable; no creamy bokeh.
recipe.treatment: No filters, no duotone, no accent overlay. Fine grain, as shot.

samples.caption: Front desk, 07:10. Available light, empty, square to the counter.
samples.prompt: The front desk of a small independent hotel at ten past seven in the morning, nobody there yet: a worn wooden counter, a closed ledger, a desk lamp off, a bell, window light from the side. Square to the counter, wide, quiet.

samples.caption: The key rack. Detail carries the ledger idea.
samples.prompt: Close detail of an old wooden key rack behind a hotel front desk, brass room keys on numbered hooks, a handwritten paper rota pinned beside it.

samples.caption: Turn-down, mid-task. Nobody looks at the camera.
samples.prompt: A housekeeper in her fifties folding white towels on a trolley in a hotel corridor, mid-task, looking down at her hands, not at the camera. Plain uniform, real and unglamorous.

samples.caption: A room between guests. One subject, space for type beside it.
samples.prompt: An empty guest room in a small independent British hotel between guests: a made bed with white linen, a wooden chair, a sash window, morning light falling across the floor. Shot square to the wall, eye level, space on the left side.

samples.caption: Back of house. The building is the subject.
samples.prompt: A back-of-house service corridor in a small hotel: a linen cupboard door ajar, stacked folded sheets on shelves, a laundry trolley, plain painted walls, window light at the far end.

misuse.caption: Don't use stock hotel photography — because every competitor does, and it shows a hotel nobody runs. Instead shoot a real property on a weekday morning.
misuse.prompt: Generic glossy stock photograph of a luxury hotel lobby with marble floors, gold fixtures, a chandelier, and a smiling receptionist in a suit posing for the camera, over-lit, perfect, corporate.

misuse.caption: Don't shoot golden hour or add a warm grade — because it turns operations into a holiday advert. Instead mid-morning window light.
misuse.prompt: A hotel terrace at golden hour with an orange sunset glow, heavy warm Instagram filter, lens flare, cocktails on the table, holiday advertising mood.

misuse.caption: Don't show people smiling at laptops — because it is the category's oldest cliché and says nothing about the house. Instead staff mid-task, away from screens.
misuse.prompt: Cliché stock photo: a smiling businesswoman at a laptop in a bright office, giving a thumbs up at the screen, coffee cup beside her, overhead fluorescent light.

photography.source: Commissioned shoot of three customer properties, one weekday morning each. Until then, the generated samples on this page are direction only — never publish them as real properties.
photography._rule: Photography is documentary: real properties, available mid-morning light, staff mid-task or empty rooms. One image per surface. Never stock, never golden hour, never type on the image.

illustration.source: Not applicable. Perch does not illustrate.
illustration.palette: Brand palette only. Illustration would never introduce a colour.
illustration.subjects: Objects, places and systems. People only at work, never posed.
illustration.never: Character illustration of any kind. Corporate-Memphis figures. Drawn metaphors for abstract concepts.
illustration.next_one: If a page feels empty, the fix is more space and fewer elements, not a drawing. Use a chart or a photograph.
illustration._rule: Perch does not illustrate. Use a chart, a photograph, or nothing. The ledger rule and the index label carry recognisability instead.

imagery.charts: Axis labels in ink.muted, gridlines in border.hairline, one accent series maximum, direct labels over a legend where they fit.

provenance._legend: stated = the founder said it · inferred = derived from what they said · assumed = filled to make the kit work, go and check
breaks_if: A second competitor starts pricing on recovered revenue rather than per property.
The primary buyer moves from the GM to the owner or the finance lead.
You move upmarket to groups above 200 rooms, where a revenue manager already exists.
provenance.expires: Revisit at the next funding round, the first marketing hire, or 3× revenue — whichever comes first.
validate: Read your last 20 closed-lost reasons and check the competitive frame.
Screenshot five competitor homepages and check the difference is not category wallpaper.
Ask three customers why they chose you over the obvious alternative, verbatim, and compare their sentence to the positioning.
